Open-redirect candidates on POST /api/v1/orders: successRedirectUrl, cancelRedirectUrl, returnUrl, refererUrl. The checkout flow sends the customer to these URLs post-authorization; if domain allowlist is missing, this is a classic phishing primitive. CVSS 6.1 (reflected) to 7.4 (stored via order id).

IDOR via webshopId on POST /api/v1/orders — the body accepts an explicit webshopId UUID that 'will ignore referrer'. If backend doesn't verify the Bearer token is scoped to that webshop, a merchant can create orders tied to another merchant's shop (and absorb the money). CVSS target 8.1-9.1.

GET /api/v1/webshop/mine leaks apiKey + testAPIKey + privateKey — the privateKey is the HMAC secret used to sign callbacks. If this endpoint is IDOR-vulnerable (same Bearer sees another merchant's data), attacker forges valid callbacks declaring Captures/Refunds on victim orders. CVSS 8.6-9.3.

API keys are HS256 JWTs with payload {name, iat}. Test (a) alg confusion (None, RS256-with-HMAC-key), (b) kid/jku/x5u header injection, (c) HS256 secret bruteforce on an exfiltrated key. If the server shares one HS256 secret across all merchants, a single secret-leak is total cross-tenant key forgery.

Customer checkout endpoint GET /api/v1/internal/checkout/begin?checkoutId=<uuid> is unauthenticated. Test checkoutId enumeration (sequential UUIDs?), session fixation, and Referer-based identity binding.
internalQrCodeId / externalQrCodeId / externalUserId fields on POST /api/v1/orders — test cross-merchant QR-code reuse (take merchant A's QR UUID, create order against it with merchant B's Bearer).
